description: Media automation troubleshooting. Is the pipeline flowing? Why can’t I reach Sonarr? Why is Plex buffering? Where is the bottleneck?

panels.description: Media containers detected by cAdvisor. Auto-populates when the media stack is deployed.

targets.expr: count(container_last_seen{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""} > (time() - 120)) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Services Running

panels.description: Media containers with failing Docker health checks.

targets.expr: count(container_health_state{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""} == 0 or container_health_state{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""} >= 2) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Health Issues

panels.description: Current throughput on the VPN container (ExpressVPN). This IS the media stack’s internet egress — all torrent traffic routes through VPN. Zero when nothing is downloading.

targets.expr: sum(rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service="vpn", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service="vpn", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: VPN Traffic

panels.description: Media containers that restarted within the time range. Frequent restarts = crash loop.

targets.expr: count(container_start_time_seconds{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""} > (time() - $__range_s)) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Recent Restarts

panels.description: All media containers with resources and uptime. Click a service to investigate on the Container Workbench or view its logs. If a service is missing from this table, it’s not running.

targets.expr: sum by (host, service) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (host, service) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""})
time() - max by (host, service) (container_start_time_seconds{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""})

sum by (host, service) (rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Media Service Status

panels.description: Current Sonarr+Radarr queue errors/warnings. Trend now lives on the Queue Depth chart above (red=errors, orange=warnings) — this stat is just today's headline number.

targets.expr: sum(sonarr_queue_error{host=~"$host"} or vector(0)) + sum(radarr_queue_error{host=~"$host"} or vector(0)) + sum(sonarr_queue_warning{host=~"$host"} or vector(0)) + sum(radarr_queue_warning{host=~"$host"} or vector(0))

panels.title: Queue Errors (Current)

panels.description: Content Sonarr/Radarr know about but haven't found yet (scraparr). A growing count with a healthy pipeline is normal (not on indexers yet); a growing count alongside indexer failures means it IS available but can't be found — check Indexer Health.
panels.title: Missing Content

panels.description: Ratio of enabled to configured Prowlarr indexers, as reported by scraparr. Prowlarr auto-disables indexers that fail repeatedly, so a ratio below 100% usually means an indexer needs attention. Note: scraparr exports counts, not a boolean healthy/unhealthy per indexer — this ratio is the closest available proxy. Uses the scalar *_total gauges rather than sum() over the per-type series, so an added label dimension can't silently double-count; the denominator is clamped so zero indexers reads 0%, not NaN. Click to check Prowlarr logs.
panels.title: Indexer Health

options.content:
**Movie not downloading?**

Use the **Trace a Title** section at the bottom of this dashboard: type the name into the `$title` box for a live merged log stream across Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, and qBittorrent.

Or [search logs in the Log Workbench →](/d/homelab-log-workbench?${__url_time_range}&var-service=sonarr&var-service=radarr&var-service=prowlarr&var-service=qbittorrent&var-service=sabnzbd)

**Common causes:**
- Queue errors → quality restrictions too tight
- Indexer down → check Indexer Health panel
- Download speed 0 → VPN issue (torrents) or provider issue (Usenet, check Per-Server Download Rate)
- Stale queue → check qBittorrent Per-Torrent Activity table

panels.description: If Plex/Jellyfin CPU is pinned → transcoding bottleneck. If Sonarr/Radarr CPU spikes → likely processing a large import or search.
panels.title: CPU per Service

panels.description: Sonarr/Radarr memory leaks are common (especially with large libraries). Watch for upward trends. Plex transcoding allocates temporary buffers that spike during playback.
panels.title: Memory per Service

panels.description: VPN container traffic = actual internet download/upload speed (all torrent traffic routes through it). Plex/Jellyfin traffic = streaming bandwidth to clients. High Sonarr/Radarr network = API calls to indexers.

targets.expr: sum by (service) (rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host", service=~"${media_services}", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Network per Service

panels.description: Which media service is writing to disk. High write rates from qBittorrent = actively downloading. High from Sonarr/Radarr = importing/moving files. Sustained high writes from Plex = thumbnail generation or transcoding temp files.
panels.title: Disk Write Rate

panels.description: Available space on NFS-mounted media volumes. Requires node_exporter on the media VM. A full NAS silently stops completed downloads from being imported. Red zone (<10% free) = immediate action needed.

defaults.noValue: NAS not mounted (requires node_exporter on media VM)

panels.title: NAS / Media Storage

panels.description:
Items queued in Sonarr/Radarr. A healthy pipeline shows brief spikes (new content added) then returns to 0. A flat non-zero line = stalled downloads. Queue errors/warnings indicate failed grabs that may need manual intervention.

Powered by scraparr (ghcr.io/thecfu/scraparr). Error/warning counts are plotted on this same chart (red/orange) instead of a separate panel.
panels.title: Queue Depth

panels.description:
qBittorrent global download/upload speed (Bps). Zero speed + non-empty queue = stalled. Check VPN container health and network. Torrent counts moved to the qBittorrent Live Torrent Activity section below (they were previously plotted here on the wrong axis).

Powered by martabal/qbittorrent-exporter (port 17871).
panels.title: Download Speed

panels.description:
SABnzbd download throughput. Usenet is not peer-limited, so this should sit near your line rate whenever the queue is non-empty. Speed near 0 with a non-empty queue means the provider connection is failing, not that there are 'no seeders' — check the Per-Server Download Rate panel to the right.

Powered by onedr0p/exportarr (port 9707).
panels.title: Usenet Download Speed

panels.description:
Queue length (jobs) and remaining bytes to fetch. A flat non-zero queue with zero speed = stalled, same failure signature as torrents.

'Warnings' is SABnzbd's own warning counter — a persistent non-zero value usually means missing articles or a failing server, which is the case for adding a fill/block provider (USENET_SERVER2_* in .env).

Powered by onedr0p/exportarr (port 9707).
panels.title: Usenet Queue

panels.description:
Bytes actually delivered by each configured Usenet server. This is how you tell whether your primary provider is carrying the load and whether a fill/block server (USENET_SERVER2_*) is being leaned on — a fill server only gets asked for articles the primary could not supply, so any sustained traffic on it means the primary is missing content.

NOTE: SABnzbd also exposes sabnzbd_server_articles_success / _total, and an obvious 'article success rate' panel would divide the two. Do not. Verified against a live download: SABnzbd reports articles_success=0 while happily pulling 30 MB/s with a single server, so that ratio reads a permanently-red 0% and sends you chasing a provider fault that does not exist. Delivered bytes is the trustworthy signal.

Powered by onedr0p/exportarr (port 9707).
panels.title: Per-Server Download Rate

options.content:
The pipeline panels above are powered by these exporters. Enable via `ENABLE_EXPORTERS=1` in `.env` (default: on).

| Exporter | What it unlocks | Image | Status |
|----------|----------------|-------|--------|
| **scraparr** | Queue depth, library size, missing content, indexer health, quality breakdown | `ghcr.io/thecfu/scraparr:latest` | Live (`media`) |
| **qbittorrent-exporter** | Download/upload speed, per-torrent progress/ETA/seeders, torrent states, ratio, free space | `martabal/qbittorrent-exporter:latest` | Live (`media:17871`) |
| **sabnzbd-exporter** | Usenet queue, speed, per-server delivered bytes | `ghcr.io/onedr0p/exportarr` | Live (`media:9707`) — was scraped but missing from Prometheus targets until now |
| **plex-exporter** | Library size/duration, streaming bandwidth, server reachability | `ghcr.io/jsclayton/prometheus-plex-exporter` | Live (`accelerated:9000`) |

**Known gap:** none of the above expose per-session transcode decisions (direct-play vs. transcode) — that needs **Tautulli**, which is a new service/deploy decision and out of scope for this dashboard pass.

**API keys:** After first deployment, retrieve from each app: Settings → General → API Key. Set `SONARR_API_KEY`, `RADARR_API_KEY`, `PROWLARR_API_KEY` in `.env` or write `config/scraparr/config.yaml`.

**Tracing tip:** Use the **Trace a Title** section at the bottom of this dashboard — type a title into the `$title` box and its grab→download→import lifecycle streams live across all services.

panels.description: Every torrent qBittorrent knows about right now — follow one download from grab to seed. 'State' is derived (this exporter has no per-torrent state string): Downloading = actively receiving, Completed = 100% and idle, Seeding = 100% and uploading, Paused/Stalled = 0% activity. ETA of 8640000s is qBittorrent's 'unknown/never' sentinel, shown as N/A.
panels.title: Per-Torrent Activity

panels.description: Real per-state torrent counts straight from qBittorrent (not derived). Zero-count states are hidden.
panels.title: Torrent State Distribution

panels.description: Free disk space (qBittorrent's own view of its download disk), global seed ratio, and current connection status (connected/firewalled/disconnected — 'firewalled' usually means port forwarding isn't reaching the client through the VPN). 'How long has a torrent been stalled' has no dedicated metric from this exporter — the state distribution panel shows the current stalled COUNT, not duration; a duration signal would need a recording rule, out of scope for this pass.
panels.title: Free Space, Ratio & Connection

panels.description: Library size and total runtime per Plex library, from the live plex-exporter job (accelerated:9000). Note: this exporter does not expose per-session transcode decisions (direct-play vs. transcode) — that needs Tautulli, which is a new service and out of scope here.
panels.title: Plex Library Stats

panels.description: Live outbound streaming bandwidth (rate of estimated_transmit_bytes_total). This is bandwidth actually being sent to clients right now, not a session count.
panels.title: Plex Streaming Bandwidth

panels.description: Plex server reachability, from the live plex-exporter job. Green = exporter scraped the server successfully; that also means Plex itself is up (the exporter can't return data from a dead server).
panels.title: Plex Server Status

panels.description: Type a movie/show name into the $title box above and watch its grab → download → import lifecycle across every media service in one merged stream. Empty $title shows everything (noisy by design — type something).
panels.title: Title Lifecycle Trace
